ledger.note: c. 1350: Tirhut occupied. 'He first occupied the Tirhut region, which he divided into two parts': 'The part north of the Budhi Gandaki River were restored to Raja Kameshwar Thakur of the Oiniwar dynasty' while 'Ilyas kept the southern part for himself, stretching from Begusarai to Nepal Terai', with headquarters at Ukkacala (Hajipur); 'Ilyas Shah also founded the city of Hajipur and first settled in 1350 AD'. The page dates Hajipur, not the occupation, and names no Delhi holder; the Oiniwar ruler who got the north back is the only holder it names, so he is the counterpart (repair 2026-10-20; was tughlaq-dynasty at confidence 1, which tughlaq-dynasty does not mirror). ledger.note: 1352: Ilyas Shah takes Sonargaon and unifies Bengal. He 'defeated the ruler of Sonargaon and unified Bengal' and 'proclaimed the establishment of the Sultanate of Bengal in 1352 through the unification of these regions', moving the capital to Pandua.
1353: Firuz Shah Tughluq occupies Pandua. 'His army occupied Pandua'; Ilyas withdrew to Ekdala fort, besieged for two months, and Bengal 'agreed to pay a tribute to the Delhi Sultan' (Bengal page).
1355: 'Firuz Shah returned to Delhi in 1355'; Ilyas 'regained control of Bengal' and pursued as far as Varanasi. The Bengal page adds that Ilyas lost 'many conquered areas' without naming them.
1359: 'Delhi again invaded Bengal' (second Ekdala); 'the Delhi forces were repulsed' and a treaty followed 'recognizing the independence' of Bengal. Start and end are the same year.
1359: the treaty after the second Ekdala siege recognises Bengal's independence.
1390: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah's reign begins and Sonargaon becomes the capital (infobox 1390-1410).

1516: the Arakan war ends ('The hostilities probably ended in 1516').

region.text: the lands up to the Tons river: Lodi's 1497 holdings between 83.2 E and 85 E (Bihar west of Bengal's block to Azamgarh)

ledger.note: c. 1523: Nasrat Shah annexes the lands up to the Tons river: 'annexed the lands up to Tons river soon after 1522', after 'the collapse of the Lodi authority in Bihar' and 'entering into an alliance with the Lohani rebels'; the page also has his Sar-i-Lashkar build a mosque in Sikandarpur, Azamgarh district, in 1527. The year is 'soon after 1522' bridged to 1523; the region is the researcher's reading (Lodi's 1497 holdings between 83.2 E and 85 E, Bihar west of Bengal's block to Azamgarh). The Tons is not in the gazetteer. Much of this land had already gone to Bahar Khan Lohani in 1519 (lodi-dynasty /ledger/13); lodi-dynasty carries the matching 1523 loss. Added to the keyframes from 1523 (repair 2026-10-20; the first notes said no page carried it).

1526: Mithila annexed. Nasrat Shah 'annexed the ruling Oiniwar dynasty in 1526 with the ruler of the Oiniwars, Laksminathasimha, being killed in battle'. Mithila is not in the gazetteer; Tirhut round Muzaffarpur is used.
1532: Turbak invades the Ahom kingdom 'with a force comprising 1,000 cavalry, 30 elephants' and guns.

October 1532: Min Bin takes Chittagong. 'On 7 October 1532 ... he led a combined invasion force of 12,000'; 'the combined invasion force defeated a Bengal army of 10,000 men and took Chittagong'. Mirrors kingdom-of-mrauk-u /ledger/6; the Mrauk U page itself ties his seizure of Chittagong to the late 1530s, so the pages disagree and the Min Bin page is followed. Removed from the keyframes from 1532 (repair 2026-10-20).

11 December 1532: 'Arakanese forces entered Dhaka on 11 December 1532 ... without a fight'; on 8 February 1533 Min Bin 'received tributes from local lords of Bengal'. Mirrors kingdom-of-mrauk-u /ledger/7 (repair 2026-10-20).

March 1533: the Ahoms win the naval battle of Duimunisila ('The invading forces lost 2,500 men, 20 ships'); Turbak was killed near the Bharali River and the Ahoms pursued to the Karatoya. No border changed.

13 April 1533: 'He left Dhaka for Mrauk-U on 13 April 1533'; 'his control of Bengal beyond Chittagong, where coins bearing his name and styling him sultan were struck, was nominal'. Mirrors kingdom-of-mrauk-u /ledger/8 (repair 2026-10-20).

region.text: Bihar, west of the Teliagarhi pass

ledger.note: March 1534: Sher Shah beats Mahmud's forces at Surajgarh ('winning a decisive victory'; Ibrahim Khan killed).

region.text: all lands west of the Teliagarhi pass

ledger.note: 1536-1537: 'Sher Shah repeatedly defeated Mahmud and took all lands west of the Teliagarhi pass'; the sultan 'held the Teliagarhi pass (1536 AD)', then paid over 13,000,000 gold coins and ceded territory up to Sakrigali. The Teliagarhi pass is not in the gazetteer; Bihar and Jharkhand stand for the land west of it.
6 April 1538: Mahmud 'finally decisively defeated by Sher Shah Suri on 6 April 1538'; Gaur sacked.

6 April 1538: the Hussain Shahi sultanate falls. Mahmud 'died of wounds sustained during the siege of Gaur'; the dynasty ended in 1538 and the succession table gives the Sur Empire. Humayun's occupation of Gaur is undated on the page.

wars.name: Ilyas Shah's Nepal raid
wars.outcome: Ilyas Shah's army 'looted Kathmandu city for three days' and sacked Swayambhunath, then returned to Bengal 'with plentiful spoils'; a raid, no hold, so no occupation event is recorded (repair 2026-10-20; the Kathmandu dossier has none).

wars.name: Delhi-Bengal war (Ekdala sieges)
wars.outcome: 1353: Firuz Shah Tughluq occupied Pandua and besieged Ilyas at Ekdala; Bengal agreed to pay tribute and lost unnamed conquests; he withdrew in 1355. 1359: the second invasion was repulsed and a treaty recognised Bengal's independence.
wars.note: The Ilyas Shah page mentions no tribute or lost areas.

wars.name: Bengal-Jaunpur War

intersect.text: the Bihar block: Bengal's 1352 shape minus its 1395 shape (Patna to Darbhanga)
north of the Ganga: a line from Buxar past Patna and Barh (25.48 N 85.72 E) to Bhagalpur

zones.text: Tirhut: the part of the Bihar block north of the Ganga (Hajipur, Muzaffarpur, Darbhanga)

wars.outcome: 'Parts of Jaunpur were annexed' (Bengal page, no place named; read as Tirhut north of the Ganga). The Ibrahim Shah Sharqi page has Ibrahim defeating Raja Ganesha in 1415 and withdrawing without annexing Bengal.

wars.name: Bengal and the Arakan wars
wars.outcome: 1429-1430 Bengali forces back Min Saw Mon and Arakan becomes a vassal; 1459 Arakan defeats Barbak Shah and takes Chittagong; 1512-1516 Hussain Shah restores Bengali sovereignty over Chittagong and northern Arakan.

wars.name: Bengal-Gajapati war of 1447-1450

zones.text: territories of Bengal west of the Ganga, including the fort of Gar Mandaran

wars.outcome: Kapilendra Deva's army took territory west of the Ganga including Gar Mandaran (Gopinathpur inscription 1447; Puri inscription 1450 'the conquest of Gauda'); no page dates a Gajapati loss of it, and Mandaran is Bengal's in 1508.

wars.name: Bengal-Kamata War

zones.text: the Kamata country up to Hajo that Cliopatria draws from 1502

wars.outcome: Muzaffar Shah's 898 AH conquest of 1492-93; the Khen dynasty overthrown in 1498; Ismail Ghazi imprisoned King Nilambar and annexed the land up to Hajo in 1499.

wars.name: Lodi invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: Sikandar Lodi invaded in 1496; the armies met at Barh and a treaty gave the country west of Barh to Lodi and left the country east of Barh with Husain Shah. The dossier draws the loss on the south bank only (the page's 1501-1502 Hussainabad mosque in trans-Gandak country shows Bengal across the Gandak).

wars.name: Bengal-Gajapati border wars
wars.outcome: Ismail Ghazi's raid reached Puri in 1508-1509 and was driven back; by 1515 Orissa was a Bengal vassal.

wars.name: Battle of Ghaghra
wars.outcome: 6 May 1529: the Mughals beat the Afghans and Bengalis but did not enter Bengal; Nasrat Shah sued for peace and kept independence.

wars.name: Gauda-Ahom War
wars.outcome: Turbak's invasion was destroyed at Duimunisila in March 1533 and he was killed near the Bharali River; no border moved.

wars.name: Arakanese invasion of Bengal
wars.outcome: 7 October 1532 Min Bin's invasion beats a Bengal army and takes Chittagong; Dhaka entered 11 December 1532 and left 13 April 1533; control beyond Chittagong nominal.

wars.name: Sher Shah Suri's conquest of Bengal

zones.text: the lands west of the Teliagarhi pass

wars.outcome: Surajgarh in March 1534; the Teliagarhi pass held in 1536; the lands west of it lost in 1536-37 with a huge indemnity; Gaur sacked on 6 April 1538.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on the pages opened; the Delhi, Jaunpur and Arakan frontiers are approximate.

The Barh treaty of 1496 is the one dated frontier on the pages ('the country west of Barh went to Sikandar Lodi'), but it is given in words, not as a line, and the page's own inscriptions (Hussainabad of Balia district 1501-1502, 'firm control ... in trans-Gandak area'; the Sikandarpur mosque of 1527) show Bengal's power across the Gandak and the Ganga further west. The loss is drawn on the south bank only and the frontier stays soft; the Assam, Orissa and Arakan frontiers are approximate.

sources.title: Bengal Sultanate
sources.note: Identity, dynasties, capitals, timeline (two readings of the same page).

sources.title: Jaunpur Sultanate
sources.note: Sixth page, read for the jaunpur-sultanate dossier; cited only for the Bihar block of 1395.

sources.title: Ibrahim Shah Sharqi
sources.note: 1415 campaign against Raja Ganesha; no 1420 annexation named (repair).

sources.title: Kingdom of Mrauk U
sources.note: Ramu 1437; vassalage 1429-1437 in the infobox (repair mirror).

sources.title: Kapilendra Deva
sources.note: 1447 and 1450 inscriptions against the Sultan of Bengal (repair mirror).

sources.title: Barh
sources.note: Coordinates of Barh, 25.48 N 85.72 E, south bank of the Ganges (repair).

notes:
Cliopatria row: 'Sultanate of Bengal' 1344-1533, nine shapes. The pages date Ilyas Shah's Lakhnauti from 1342 and the unification from 1352 (start = 1342, new 1342 keyframe), and the end to 6 April 1538 (Mahmud Shah page; the Bengal page's infobox runs 'ended 1576' through Sur and Karrani Afghan rule, which is left to the Sur Empire row and a possible Karrani dossier). Cliopatria's 1534-1538 gap is filled by a new keyframe.
Shape problems: no Chittagong (Bengali 1340-1459 and 1516 on, Arakan's in between) and no Sylhet in any shape; Khulna and Jessore present from 1352 against the page's 1459; the Bihar block lost 1395 and regained 1482 with no Bengal page for either; the Kamata block is drawn from 1502 (page: 1499) and dropped from 1512 although Kamrup is in Hussain Shah's realm in 1519; Orissa drawn from 1512 (page: vassal by 1515). The corrections add or remove those blocks. No area appears on any page.
Pages disagree: dynasty dates (Ganesha 1414 or 1415, restored Ilyas Shahi 1435 or 1433, Habshi 1487 or 1486, Hussain Shahi 1494 or 1493); the capital's move to Gaur 1433 (infobox) or 1450 (article); the Barh treaty giving Lodi the land west of Barh against a 1501-1502 inscription across the Gandak and the 1527 Azamgarh mosque (Nasrat page) holding 'the Jaunpuri territory annexed by his father'; the Ilyas Shah page denies the tribute and lost areas the Bengal page gives for 1353; Nasrat's reign 1519-1533 (page) against 1532.
Not recorded for lack of a dated page: Nasrat Shah's annexation of lands up to the Tons river 'soon after 1522' (allied with the Lohani rebels); the Arakanese invasion of 1532-1533 recorded in the Mrauk U dossier; Chittagong's 1534 Portuguese factory; Humayun's occupation of Gaur; Mandaran and Midnapore; the Tripura expeditions' dates; the end of the Tripura and Orissa vassalages (no vassal_end events: the pages give none, so both are left running to the state's end in 1538, the validator's 'fine only if' case).
Counterparts that need dossiers: lakhnauti-sultanate, sonargaon-sultanate (Mubarak Shahi), satgaon-sultanate (Ilyas's own realm before 1352), kingdom-of-tripura (Twipra), oiniwar-dynasty (Mithila, to 1526), a Kamata kingdom (Khen dynasty, to 1498). Page budget (5) used: Bengal Sultanate, Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah, Alauddin Hussain Shah, Nasiruddin Nasrat Shah, Ghiyasuddin Mahmud Shah (the Jaunpur page was read for another dossier). Gazetteer: Pandua, Gaur, Sonargaon, Teliagarhi, Barh, Mithila, Mandaran, Kachar are not in it; coordinates for the capitals are the sites' own, not on the pages.

Repair 2026-10-20 (reviewer sa-04-c): the Bihar block is split at the Ganga. Tirhut (north) is Bengal's from 1420 (gain from Jaunpur, confidence 1: the Bengal page names no place), the south bank from 1482; Jaunpur's 1395 gain names this dossier for the block and jaunpur-sultanate now runs to 1494 so the 1482 counterpart exists. The 1496 Barh treaty is drawn as a loss of the south-bank country west of Barh to Lodi (the north bank stays Bengal's on the strength of the 1501-1502 Hussainabad inscription). Nasrat Shah's annexation up to the Tons river (c. 1523, Nasrat page) is added; the earlier notes were wrong that no page carried it. Mirrors added from the neighbours' pages: Ramu 1437 and the 1532-1533 Arakanese invasion (Chittagong, Dhaka occupation) from kingdom-of-mrauk-u; the Gajapati campaign of 1447-1450 is a contest, not a loss (see event note). The 1346 Nepal sack is a raid and its occupation events are removed. The Tirhut event of c. 1350 now names oiniwar-dynasty. The 1395-1481 keyframe is split at 1420, 1437 and 1459, and the later ones at 1496, 1523 and 1532, so that each ledger event shows in the shapes. Disagreement kept: the Mrauk U infobox ends Arakan's vassalage in 1437, the Bengal page in 1459 (ledger /vassal_end 1459 kept). Not done: vassal_end for Tripura and Orissa (no page opened dates them).
